title: The Gift That Cannot Be Bought

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A trader offers a fortune for a family's carved paddle: sell it, or explain that some things have no price.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A trader has seen the old carved paddle hanging in (subject)'s hut, the one (subject.his/her) great-grandparent made, and has offered more for it than (subject)'s family earns in a year. (subject) is tempted: the roof leaks and the canoe is cracked. (friend), (subject.his/her) grandparent, says nothing, and waits. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) sells the paddle. The roof is fixed and the canoe is new. (friend) never mentions the paddle again. But on the evening the trader leaves, (subject) finds (friend.him/her) sitting by the empty hook on the wall.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) explains to the trader that the paddle is not for sale, at any price. The trader cannot understand it. (friend) does not say anything, but that evening (friend.he/she) tells (subject) the whole story of the paddle, for the first time.
